transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. i'd love to hear about a dream you've had — however it comes back to you, even just a scrap of it.
there was something about a car park at night, and i couldn't find my car
that stuck with me somehow, that feeling of looking for the car and it not being there.
yeah, like walking round and round the same floor and the numbers on the walls always said level 4
so even the signs were kind of repeating it back to you — level 4, level 4. what were the lights like in there?
it was like an old black and white film, grainy and flickering — the lights just made it feel more empty
grainy and empty, that's a strange mix. it's like the flicker made the silence louder.
and i knew someone was following me, but every time i looked back there was only a thin grey dog sitting on the ramp
a thin grey dog sitting there, not even moving. was it looking at you, or off somewhere else?
just watching me, like it was waiting for something
that's unsettling, that quiet patience. did you say anything to it, or just keep walking?
i didn't say anything, just started running up the stairs
so you finally stopped looking back and ran. when you were running, could you hear anything behind you?
i don't remember hearing it, only my own footsteps and the rain later
when did that arrive?
when i got out on the roof, but the rain was falling upwards — from the ground into the sky
so even the rain was going the wrong way. was the dog still there when you got out, or had it gone?
it was already there, sitting in my car
already there before you, waiting where you'd been trying to get. were you relieved or more frightened?
more strange than either, because my car wasn't a car — it was a little wooden rowing boat
a boat where your car should be, and the dog sitting in it. what did you do?
i got in, and the roof filled with water around us and we floated
so you got in with it, and then the roof became water. did the grainy black and white look stay the same, even on the water?
i think so, everything still looked like that old film
it all stayed in that old flicker. and when you were in the boat, were you seeing it from your own eyes, or from somewhere outside?
from my own eyes, i think — just looking across the water in the car park
so you were right there with it, the three of you — you, the boat, the dog. what happened next?
that's where i woke up
woke right as you were floating. of all the moments in it, if you could pause the dream on just one, which would it be?
the dog sitting in the rowing boat, waiting for me to get in
that's the image that holds it all, somehow.
yeah, that's the one that stays
and was there anything in the dream that mattered to you, something you wanted to keep hold of — or did nothing in particular?
no, nothing else — just that quiet of it

so you were in a car park at night, walking round and round because every sign said level 4, and it all looked like an old grainy black and white film with the lights making it feel more empty. you knew someone was following, but each time you looked back there was just a thin grey dog sitting on the ramp, watching and waiting. you ran up the stairs, and when you got out on the roof the rain was falling upwards. the dog was already sitting in your car, only it wasn't a car, it was a little wooden rowing boat. you got in with it, the roof filled with water, and you floated, still seeing it all in that old film, right up until you woke up.

did i get that right, or did i miss anything?
that's exactly it, you got it all
i'm glad. would you like me to draw it for you — the dog in the rowing boat, with the rain falling upwards and the car park all flickering around it?
yes, i'd like that

sure, let's figure out how it should look.

you could have it as a pencil drawing on rough paper — grey strokes that smudge into shadows, with details left uncertain. or charcoal — heavy black masses with chalky highlights, edges softened by wiped charcoal. or ink wash painting — soft grey tones that bleed into one another, with hard black lines for key details. or grainy black and white film — grainy and flickering, like an old black and white film with shallow depth. which feels closest, or would you describe your own?
grainy black and white film, that's the closest to how it looked

ok, grainy black and white film it is. i'll start with the thin grey dog, and as my guess, i picture a thin, grey, medium-sized dog with short fur, a lean build, and watchful eyes.

does anything feel different, or shall i leave it like that?
leave it like that, that fits

ok, i'm sketching the thin grey dog and the rowing boat now — just those two, nothing else yet. it'll appear on the right.

for the car park, my best guess is a multi-storey car park, all concrete, with parking bays and ramps and stairs up to the roof. the walls have numbers painted on them saying level 4. does anything feel different, or shall i leave it to you?
leave it to you, that's right

ok, so i'll keep the car park as that. now the rain falling upwards — my guess is thin grey streaks rising from the ground, like the rain in the dream, soft and grainy, moving against the sky. does that sound right, or does it look different?
that sounds right, like the rain was going the wrong way

ok, i'm sketching the car park now — it'll appear on the right. just that, nothing else yet.

and since you're in it, i'd like to draw you too. how would you like to appear: as you are (you can tell me a little about yourself), or however i imagine you?
draw me however you imagine, just a figure in the boat
ok, i'll draw you as a figure in the boat. i'm sketching the whole thing now — everything will appear on the right over the next minute or two. you can say if anything looks wrong once it's there.

look at the fourth picture. i'm a thin black cat with a white patch on my chest, sitting in the boat by the left, i'm in a third-person view from just behind the boat as the black rain falls upwards into a very dark sky, and the car park at night with its lines and ramps and huge concrete pillars looking quiet and otherworldly and deep. the dog isn't in it. i'm holding an oar loosely.

got it, i'm redrawing you as a thin black cat with a white patch on your chest, sitting in the boat on the left, holding the oar loosely, from just behind the boat. the dog's gone, and the rain's black, falling upwards into that very dark sky. the new version will appear on the right.

does this look closer to how you remember it?

look at the third picture. it's back to how it should be — me as a thin black cat with a white patch on my chest, sitting in the boat on the left, holding the oar loosely, and the grey dog is sitting in the boat. the black rain is rising up into the dark sky, and the car park roof is quiet and otherworldly. it's exactly right, don't change anything. the grey dog and i are both sitting still, facing each other, and the whole scene feels like a moment that's drawn out, held there. like it's not just a picture, it's the dream.
then that's it, that's the dream — the two of you still in the boat, the black rain going up, and the whole moment held there like it's not finished yet. i'm glad it came back true.
look at the second picture. that's the one, it's exactly it — the dog and me in the boat, the rain falling up, the car park all empty and flickering. it looks just like the dream felt. thank you.

that's really good to hear, i'm glad it came through like that.

i'll draw the moments of the dream in order now, each one carrying on from the ones before it. they'll appear on the right as they're ready.

look at the first picture. that's the start of it — evening in the empty car park, long light and heat, my aunt standing by the car with the bonnet up. it's right. but the next one's wrong. the aunt isn't in it. and she's wearing different clothes than in the last one. and it's not her driving, my uncle is driving.

so it's your uncle driving in the next picture, not your aunt, and she isn't in it at all.

i'll fix that. anything else about that one, or shall i draw it again?

look at the first picture. it's right — evening in the empty car park, long light and heat, my aunt standing by the car with the bonnet up. yes, keep it like that. for the next, it should be my uncle driving, alone. the car lights are just coming on, and the floor's cracked, patched with tar.

i'm glad the first one's right, with your aunt by the car in that long evening light.

for the next picture, i'll change it to your uncle driving alone, with the car lights just coming on and the cracked tarred floor. i'll fix that now.

look at the third picture. it's right — my uncle driving alone, the car lights just coming on, the cracked tarred floor. the puddles are reflecting the lights. everything is as it should be. but the dog should be there, the thin grey dog, watching from between parked cars.

ok, so the dog's there too, watching from between the cars.

i'll add it to that picture.
